document.title: Anatoly Chernyaev Diary, October 17, 1985
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan and the Soviet Withdrawal 1989 20 Years Later
document.note: At the Politburo session of Oct 17, 1985, Gorbachev proposed a final decision on Afghanistan, quoted citizens' letters on dissatisfaction with the war, and described telling Karmal 'we will help you, but with arms only, not troops.' Chernyaev noted Gorbachev's negative reaction to Defense Minister Sokolov's assessment.

persons.name: Anatoly Chernyaev
persons.role: Soviet official and diarist; attended the Politburo session

mentions.quote: I was at the Politburo today. There was a historical statement about Afghanistan.

persons.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
persons.role: Soviet General Secretary; decided to end the Soviet involvement in Afghanistan

mentions.quote: Gorbachev has finally made up his mind to put an end to it.
With or without Karmal we will follow this line firmly, which must in a minimally short amount of time lead to our withdrawal

persons.name: Babrak Karmal
persons.role: Afghan (PDPA) leader whom Gorbachev told to prepare to defend the regime without Soviet troops by summer 1986

mentions.quote: [Gorbachev] outlined his talk with Karmal. He, Gorbachev said, was dumbfounded

persons.name: Sergei Sokolov
persons.role: Marshal of the Soviet Union, defense minister; spoke twice at the Politburo

mentions.quote: Marshal Sokolov took the floor twice, and it was obvious that he was ready to pull out of there

persons.name: Andrei Gromyko
persons.role: Soviet Politburo member who proposed amendments to recommendations for Karmal

mentions.quote: Gromyko took the floor, pronounced some amendments to the recommendations that are supposed to be handed over to Karmal

events.description: Politburo session at which Gorbachev announced his decision to end the Soviet involvement in Afghanistan and withdraw.
Gorbachev's talk with Karmal, in which he said Afghan forces must defend the revolution themselves by summer 1986.
Politburo session at which Gorbachev reported his conversation with Karmal and announced a firm course toward withdrawal from Afghanistan.
Gorbachev's talk with Karmal, telling him the Soviets would not stay forever and he must broaden the regime base.
Gorbachev stated 'With or without Karmal we will follow this line firmly' toward withdrawal from Afghanistan.
Deadline set by Gorbachev for Afghan leadership to defend its revolution without Soviet troops.
Gromyko proposed amendments to recommendations to be handed to Karmal in a day or two.

key_claims: Gorbachev decided at the 17 Oct 1985 Politburo to put an end to the Soviet involvement in Afghanistan.
Gorbachev told Karmal that by summer 1986 the Afghans would have to defend their revolution themselves.
Soviet help would continue only as aviation, artillery and equipment, not soldiers.
Karmal was urged to broaden the regime's base, drop socialism, restore Islam and share power with hostile band leaders.
Letters from Soviet citizens criticizing the war informed the Politburo discussion.
Marshal Sokolov was ready to pull out and had no indulgence for Karmal.
